draft.title: The fall of the Bastille
card: The Bastille was a royal fortress and prison in Paris. It stood for the king's power, and it held few prisoners in 1789.
In July 1789 the king moved troops towards Paris and dismissed the minister Necker. Many Parisians feared the crown would use force against the new National Assembly.
On 14 July a crowd searched for gunpowder and weapons. It first took muskets from the Invalides, then attacked the Bastille, where the governor surrendered after fighting.
The crown had lost control of the capital. The event showed that Parisians would act by force, and 14 July became a symbol of the revolution.
draft.remember: The Bastille fell because Parisians feared the king's troops and wanted weapons, and its fall showed the crown could not control Paris.

a.q: Why was the fall of the Bastille important for the crown?
opts: It showed the crown could no longer control Paris
It freed many political prisoners held by the king
It ended the royal power to tax the Third Estate
It forced the king to call the Estates-General
a.why: The crowd took a royal fortress by force, and the king's authority in the capital failed. The Bastille held few prisoners, so freeing prisoners was not the main result. The Estates-General had already met in May 1789.
a.clue: Think about what the attack showed about the king's power in Paris.

b.q: Which best explains why the crowd attacked the Bastille on 14 July 1789?
opts: They wanted gunpowder and feared royal troops near Paris
They wanted to end the Estates-General and restore the king
They wanted to punish the clergy for holding privileges
They wanted to free the many prisoners held there
b.why: Parisians feared the troops and the dismissal of Necker, and they searched for weapons and gunpowder. The Bastille held only a few prisoners, so freeing many prisoners is the tempting but wrong choice. The crowd was not trying to end the Estates-General or attack the clergy.
b.clue: Think about what the crowd feared and what they needed to defend themselves.

a.best: It showed the crown could no longer control Paris

b.best: They wanted gunpowder and feared royal troops near Paris

problems.detail: The clue ('what the attack showed about the king's power in Paris') almost restates the right option. It is the only option that mentions Paris or what the event 'showed', so a student can match words instead of knowing the idea.

The clue ('what the crowd feared and what they needed to defend themselves') points straight to the only option that contains 'feared' and names a supply the crowd needed (gunpowder), giving the answer away.

proposal.title: The fall of the Bastille
card: The Bastille was a royal fortress and prison in Paris. It stood for the king's power, but it held only a few prisoners in 1789.

By July 1789 the Estates-General had already met and become the National Assembly. The king then moved troops towards Paris and dismissed the minister Necker, so many Parisians feared the crown would use force.
On 14 July a crowd searched for weapons and gunpowder. It first took muskets from the Invalides, then attacked the Bastille, where the governor surrendered after fighting.
The crown had lost control of the capital. The event showed that Parisians would act by force, and 14 July became a symbol of the revolution.
proposal.remember: Fear of royal troops and a hunt for gunpowder led to the attack, and its success showed the king no longer held Paris.

a.q: Why was the fall of the Bastille important for the crown?
opts: It showed the crown had lost control of Paris
It showed most Parisians still backed the king
It freed many political prisoners held in Paris
It forced the king to call the Estates-General
a.why: A crowd took a royal fortress by force, and the king's authority in the capital failed. Freeing prisoners is tempting, but the Bastille held only a few. The Estates-General had already met before July 1789.
a.clue: Check the order of events in 1789, and what the fortress held.

b.q: Which best explains why the crowd attacked the Bastille on 14 July 1789?
opts: They sought gunpowder and feared an attack by royal troops
They sought to free the many political prisoners held there
They sought to stop the Assembly and feared losing the king
They sought to punish nobles and feared losing their land
b.why: The king had moved troops near Paris and dismissed Necker, so Parisians feared force and hunted for weapons and gunpowder. Freeing many prisoners is the tempting wrong choice, as the Bastille held only a few. The crowd was defending the Assembly, not trying to stop it.
b.clue: What had the crowd already taken earlier that same day?

a.best: It showed the crown had lost control of Paris

b.best: They sought gunpowder and feared an attack by royal troops
